investigations.name: complex-geometry
investigations.description:
Wraps a single `ComplexGeometryStep` in the `complex_geometry` composite
generator (Task 11). The Step is stateless -- given only a named geometry
+ mesh resolution + polynomial degree, it: (1) builds the geometry with
the real gmsh Python API (`viva_fenics.fem_gmsh`) -- constructive solid
geometry (`gmsh.model.occ`) boolean cuts producing an obstacle domain
(unit square minus a circular hole), an L-shaped domain (unit square minus
its upper-right quadrant), or an annulus (outer disk minus a concentric
inner disk); (2) imports the resulting unstructured triangulation into a
dolfinx `Mesh` via `dolfinx.io.gmsh.model_to_mesh(gmsh.model, comm, rank,
gdim=2)`; and (3) solves the Poisson equation -Laplacian(u) = 1 with a
homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition on the FULL exterior boundary
(including the inner hole boundary for obstacle/annulus) -- a real
`dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem` assembled and solved on the imported
mesh's true cells, not the unit square every other study in this
investigation uses.

This is an ADVANCED, showcase-tier study: it is the investigation's only
demonstration that the FEniCSx bridge works on genuinely non-trivial,
gmsh-generated domain topologies (a hole, a re-entrant corner, a
multiply-connected ring), not just the unit square's built-in structured
triangulation every other study relies on.

investigations.name: mesh-convergence
investigations.description:
Reuses `PoissonSolverStep` (as `poisson-validation` does) but at
degree=1 and swept over `resolution`, via the `mesh_convergence` composite
generator -- one composite build per sweep point (the sweep itself lives
in this study's `variants:`/runner, not in the generator, which
parameterizes a single (resolution, degree) pair). `fem.build_mesh` uses
dolfinx's "crossed" triangulation specifically to avoid a known P1
superconvergence artifact on the default "right" diagonal that would
collapse the error to round-off at every resolution and mask the true
rate.

investigations.name: moving-boundary
investigations.description:
Wraps a single `MovingBoundaryProcess` in the `moving_boundary` composite
generator. Each tick, the process advances the mesh motion and diffusion
field by `dt`-sized substeps: (1) evaluate the prescribed boundary law
`y_top(t)` (`mode="oscillate"`: `1 + amplitude*sin(omega*t)`;
`mode="grow"`: `1 + amplitude*t`), (2) mutate `domain.geometry.x` in
place -- a uniform vertical stretch of the reference (t=0) unit-square
y-coordinates, mapping the fixed bottom boundary to y=0 and the moving
top boundary to y=y_top(t) -- and (3) re-assemble and re-solve a
backward-Euler diffusion step with a fresh `dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem`
on that deformed geometry. This is the PRESCRIBED-mesh-motion ALE
fallback explicitly sanctioned for this showcase (real dolfinx geometry
mutation + a genuine re-solve every substep on the true deformed cells --
not a mock, not a cosmetic coordinate transform after the fact). Because
only the domain's height changes (width stays 1), the FEM-assembled
`domain_measure` (`integral(1) dx` over the current mesh) should equal
`boundary_position` to near machine precision -- a strong,
non-tautological cross-check that the mesh geometry really was mutated.

This is an ADVANCED, showcase-tier study: it is the investigation's only
deforming-domain demo, and the first process whose mesh itself (not just
its solution field) is time-varying state.

investigations.name: navier-stokes
investigations.description:
Wraps a single `NavierStokesProcess` in the `navier_stokes` composite
generator. Each tick, the process advances the lid-driven cavity flow by
`dt`-sized IPCS substeps: (1) a tentative-velocity solve (Crank-Nicolson
diffusion, explicit convection via the previous step's velocity), (2) a
pressure-correction Poisson solve using the tentative velocity's
divergence as a source, (3) a velocity-correction solve using the
pressure correction's gradient. All three are real
`dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem` direct solves -- no reimplementation of
the physics, no mock. `velocity_x`/`velocity_y`/`pressure`/
`speed_integral` are `overwrite` sensor outputs (the process's own
internally-persisted absolute flow state, freshly reported each tick),
mirroring `DiffusionProcess.integral`'s convention.

This is an ADVANCED, showcase-tier study within the investigation: it is
the first fluid-dynamics (as opposed to scalar diffusion/reaction) demo,
and the first to couple two different function spaces (P2 velocity, P1
pressure) in one process.

investigations.name: poisson-validation
investigations.description:
Wraps a single `PoissonSolverStep` (Task 2) in the `poisson_baseline`
composite generator. The Step is stateless -- given only mesh resolution +
polynomial degree, it builds the mesh, solves -Laplacian(u) = -6 subject to
the manufactured solution's Dirichlet boundary values, and reports both the
nodal solution and its L2 error against the exact solution
u = 1 + x^2 + 2*y^2.

investigations.name: reaction-diffusion
investigations.description:
This is the investigation's composability showcase. `DiffusionProcess`
(Task 3) and `LogisticReactionProcess` (Task 4) are coupled PURELY through
shared stores: `stores.solution` is read+written by `DiffusionProcess` and
read by `LogisticReactionProcess`; `stores.source` is written by
`LogisticReactionProcess` (`overwrite[array[float]]` -- a fresh per-tick
rate, not an accumulated delta) and read by `DiffusionProcess`, which
multiplies it by dt internally. Swap `LogisticReactionProcess` for any
other process that reads "solution" and writes "source" and
`DiffusionProcess` is none the wiser -- that substitutability is the
claim this study exists to demonstrate, du/dt = D*laplacian(u) +
r*u*(1-u/K) emerging from composition, not from either process
implementing Fisher-KPP itself.

investigations.name: transient-diffusion
investigations.description:
Wires a single `DiffusionProcess` (Task 3) to shared `stores.solution`/
`stores.source` and a `RAMEmitter`, seeded with a nodal gaussian bump. The
process returns a DELTA each tick (new field - previous field) so the
shared `array[float]` store composes additively -- the same convention
`reaction-diffusion` (this investigation's headline study) relies on to
couple a second process into `stores.source`.
